text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria police raise to four million from one million naira reward for information that will lead to arrest of persons behind spate of recent bomb blasts in the country.
- The provisional ruling council discusses security and state of the nation at Wednesday's meeting in the capital Abuja and is to reconvene in a fortnight, says its spokesman.

- Soldiers have now been withdrawn from the streets of the midwestern oil city of Warri, which was rocked by ethnic clashes over the relocation of the local council for many weeks until early May when the army moved in to restore order.
- Nigerian pilots association backs government's tough stand in its face-off with Britain over the two nations' mutual ban on each other's aircraft.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani directs that all government property should be insured with state firm, the National Insurance Corporation of Nigeria.
- Detectives investigating recent bomb explosions in Nigeria say the motive is to cause disaffection within the armed forces and to set junior military officers against federal government.
- Electoral commission publishes comprehensive list of federal and state constituencies for next round of elections.
- Lagos state appoints 10 commissioners, two of them women, for its executive council.
- Nigeria and the United States may disagree over the vexed issues of a new capital structure and voting rights at the Africa Development Bank which is holding its annual general meeting in Abidjan.
- Nigeria gives Britain fresh condition to end ban on each other's aircraft; says ban on Nigeria Airways flights to London must be lifted for negotiations to end the face-off to proceed.
- Nigeria negotiates with soldiers who seized power in Sierra Leone to restore democracy.
- Neighbouring Benin slashes duty on rice to tempt Nigerian importers to use its port.
